text:
sara: Heads up: CI pipeline leaked a Vault token in helm post-renderer logs. Found in artifact storage. :facepalm:

jamal: Wtf — how did helm log that? We're using a post-renderer script to call `vault kv get` for templating.

alex: Do we have the token value? Need to revoke asap. Who's CI runner used? gh-actions/self-hosted?

sara: GHA self-hosted runners in prod. The script does: `VAULT_TOKEN=$VAULT_TOKEN vault kv get -format=json secret/chart/foo` and we echo the output for debugging — my bad.

kevin: Revoke token now. Also rotate any service tokens that might have been exposed. @vault-bot can you block the token id?

vault-bot: Received. Token revoked (masked). Any artifacts with token will be flagged for retention purge.

sara: Thanks. But there's another fallout: the post-renderer also wrote a secret manifest into the `manifests/` artifact, which got picked up by the gitops bot and created a sealed-secret with the wrong sops KMS alias, so sealed-secrets controller in eu-west can't decrypt -> secret missing in eu-west -> inference pods failing to start on GPU pool.

jamal: :eyes: So we leaked plain secret + created sealed secret with wrong KMS alias? That's a cascade.

alex: Symptoms? Pod events?

sara: Pods stuck init: unable to mount secret 'model-creds' -> secret not found. On ray-inference nodes. Cluster autoscaler brought nodes, but pods can't schedule.

kevin: Action items: 1) purge artifacts and mark audit 2) revoke token + rotate creds 3) fix pipeline to not emit secrets 4) remediate sealed secret in eu-west so pods can get creds.

jamal: Quick fix: re-create secret in eu-west from vault via an on-cluster job using Vault Agent + Kubernetes auth. That avoids reusing CI token.

alex: Long term: pipeline shouldn't do live calls to Vault during helm rendering that end up in artifacts. Use sops-encrypted values checked into repo + sealed-secrets or use external-secrets/operator to sync.

sara: Proposed patch: in GH Action remove `echo` logs, mask VAULT_TOKEN and avoid uploading raw manifests. Example:

```
- name: Mask VAULT_TOKEN
  run: echo "::add-mask::$VAULT_TOKEN"
- name: Render templates
  run: |
    vault kv get -format=json secret/chart/foo > /tmp/secret.json
    jq -r '.data.password' /tmp/secret.json | sops --encrypt - > chart/secret.sops
```

Also stop uploading raw `manifests/` to artifacts.

kevin: Also update GitOps: block automated import of artifacts that contain `sops` or `vault` keywords. Add artifact scanner.

jamal: Add a lint step: fail if any rendered manifest contains `kind: Secret` with plaintext `data:` fields.

alex: I'll open a quick PR for the GH action changes + lint job. @sara can you add remediation runbook steps?

sara: On it. Draft runbook in #incidents with steps: revoke token, purge artifact, re-create secret via on-cluster job, patch gitops, escalate to security.

vault-bot: Recommend switching to Kubernetes auth for Vault in CI runners via short-lived role tokens. Use vault-agent with template sink in-cluster.

deploy-bot: CI runner updated to mask secrets; artifact purge initiated; gitops queue paused for eu-west. Notifying on-call eng-sre.

kevin: One more: check if any model pods logged secrets into stdout on crash. Search logs for `VAULT_TOKEN=` across pods in last 24h.

jamal: I'll run cluster-wide grep. If found, rotate creds for impacted models.

sara: Thanks all. Postmortem after stabilization. Lessons: never hydrate secrets in CI artifacts, prefer sealed/secrets or in-cluster retrieval, and add linting to prevent secret manifests in rendered output.
